title: A Hierarchical Architecture for Embodied Intelligence Systems: Enabling Embodied Intelligence Through Layered Decoupling and Unified Standards
content: Embodied intelligence, at the frontier where artificial intelligence extends into the physical world, has become a major focus of both academia and industry. Its rapid expansion, however, has exposed serious challenges, including system complexity, tight hardware--software coupling, and barriers to industrial deployment. The field needs a general system architecture that can accommodate heterogeneous robot embodiments, control mechanisms, and cognitive reasoning models. To address this need, we propose the Embodied Intelligence System Level Hierarchy (EISLH). Inspired by the layered abstractions that enabled the widespread adoption of computer systems, EISLH decouples the embodied-intelligence stack into five functional levels: (1) User Command and Physical Environment, (2) Embodied Compiler (EC), (3) Embodied Instruction Set Architecture (EISA), (4) Embodied Action Executor (EAE), and (5) Embodied Hardware. By defining common standards at each level, the architecture turns a conventionally monolithic, tightly coupled system into a modular structure whose components can evolve independently. It thereby provides a reference for standardization in embodied intelligence and encourages an open, modular, and extensible architectural paradigm.
